title: Pythagorean Theorem
explanation: The Pythagorean Theorem relates the lengths of the sides of a right triangle. The square of the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares of the two legs.

title: Quadratic Formula
explanation: The Quadratic Formula is used to find the solutions of a quadratic equation in the form ax^2 + bx + c = 0.

title: Slope Formula
explanation: The Slope Formula calculates the steepness and direction of a line using two points.

title: Distance Formula
explanation: The Distance Formula calculates the distance between two points on a coordinate plane.

title: Midpoint Formula
explanation: The Midpoint Formula finds the point exactly halfway between two points on a coordinate plane.

title: Point-Slope Form
explanation: Point-Slope Form represents a linear equation using the slope of the line and a known point on the line.

title: Slope-Intercept Form
explanation: Slope-Intercept Form represents a linear equation using its slope and y-intercept.

title: Arithmetic Sequence
explanation: The formula for an arithmetic sequence finds the nth term by adding a constant common difference to the first term repeatedly.

title: Geometric Sequence
explanation: The formula for a geometric sequence finds the nth term by multiplying the first term by a common ratio raised to the appropriate power.

title: Arithmetic Series
explanation: The Arithmetic Series Formula calculates the sum of the first n terms of an arithmetic sequence.

title: Geometric Series
explanation: The Geometric Series Formula calculates the sum of the first n terms of a geometric sequence when the common ratio is not 1.

title: Simple Interest
explanation: The Simple Interest Formula calculates the interest earned or charged based on the principal, interest rate, and time.

title: Compound Interest
explanation: The Compound Interest Formula calculates the accumulated amount when interest is compounded at regular intervals.

title: Permutations
explanation: The Permutation Formula counts the number of ways to arrange r objects selected from n objects when order matters.

title: Combinations
explanation: The Combination Formula counts the number of ways to select r objects from n objects when order does not matter.

title: Probability of an Event
formula: P(A)=\frac{\text{Number of favorable outcomes}}{\text{Total number of possible outcomes}}
explanation: The Probability Formula determines how likely an event is to occur by comparing favorable outcomes with all possible outcomes.

title: Mean
explanation: The Mean Formula calculates the average of a set of numerical values by dividing their sum by the number of values.

title: Area of a Circle
explanation: The Area of a Circle Formula calculates the amount of space inside a circle using its radius.

title: Volume of a Cylinder
explanation: The Volume of a Cylinder Formula calculates the three-dimensional space inside a cylinder using its radius and height.

title: Law of Sines
explanation: The Law of Sines relates the side lengths of a triangle to the sines of their opposite angles and can be used to solve oblique triangles.
